Access, bins and numbering.

If entered, this house is automatically flagged as gated on Routes and Maps, visible to you and your crew.

The permanent bin number. Leave it blank and you can assign the next available one from Customer Numbers. Normally left blank — the number is picked for you from Measured Feet.     Who Pays for Whom

    Every bill that covers more than one house. The customer sees this same list in their portal and on their RSVP email. A house is on somebody else’s bill when its Bill To Phone is filled in, or when two houses share one phone number. Houses that said No for this season are not billed and are not listed.

    Fill in missing towns

    Some customers came in with no town on their record — usually an address that ends “, UT” with the town missing. They can never be put on a route, because every route day is one town. This reads the town back off the map pin that is already on their record. It only ever fills a blank in; nothing that already has a town is touched.

    Works in batches of 50 so it never locks the page up. Press Check First, look at it, fill them in — then press Check First again for the next 50. It always picks up where it left off.

    Creates or updates customer records here first, so Routes, Invoices, Quotes, and the Customers list all stay in sync automatically from this one import.

    Day to day: connect your master sheet once, then press Compare and tick what is right. Everything else on this page is for one-off jobs — pasting a single column, or importing with invoices — and is folded away below.

    Paste the whole master sheet

    Select the sheet in Excel — heading row and all — copy, and paste it in here. It reads the headings, works out which column is which, and fills in the boxes below for you. Nothing is saved until you press Check First and then Import, same as always.

    ① Where the sheet comes from

    Pick your master sheet once on this computer and it is read straight from OneDrive every time — no pasting. Or paste it into the box above instead, for a one-off.

    ② Compare it with the website

    Changes nothing on its own. Lists who is on the sheet but not on the website, who is on the website but not on the sheet, and every field the two disagree about — then you tick what is right and sync it. This is the one to use.

    Paste one column at a time, or import with invoices

    These fill themselves in from the box above. You only need to touch them if you are pasting one column on its own, or tocheck what landed where before importing. Row 1 in every box must be the same customer. We always geocode within Utah, and update an existing customer instead of duplicating them when the phone or street already matches.

    THE ONE THAT MATTERS. This is who each row is — every other box is matched to this one, so its row count is the count everything else has to agree with. A number here finds that customer whatever their address or town says. It is only used to find them, never changed. To give somebody a different number, open them in All Customers and edit it there, where the old number goes back in the pool and the new one comes out of it.

    Tick this if your sheet reads Cattani Julie or Cattani, Julie and the site should show Julie Cattani. Only the first word moves to the end, so “Beckstead Paul /Jill” stays together. Press Check First afterwards and read the Name column — a business like “Lehi Vision Care” would be turned round too, and that is the one thing to look out for.

    For backfilling real enrollment dates — leave blank to use today's date. Any typed date format works (e.g. 1/15/2023 or 2023-01-15).

    Same 9 options as the Add Customer form — Warm White, Pure White, Red, Green, Blue, Purple, Orange, Pink, Multi. Separate multiple colors on one line with a comma or a slash. Just list the colors for a plain mix (e.g. Red, Green). Repeat a color to specify an exact alternating pattern (e.g. Red, Red, Warm White, Warm White) — it's detected automatically and shows as a badge on that customer's Routes & Customers row. Leave blank to leave their existing colors/pattern untouched.

    Fill this in and an invoice is created/updated automatically under that row's phone number — no need for the Invoice Fields box below unless you're billing someone to a different phone.

    Type October, November, or Any — not case-sensitive. Leave blank for Any.

    Type White or Green — not case-sensitive. Blank leaves it unchanged.

    Type Yes or No (y/n also works). Blank leaves it unchanged.

    Type Yes or No (y/n also works). Blank leaves it unchanged.

    The # Feet column off the master sheet. This is the one that drives everything else — how many bins the house needs, how many bundles the warehouse builds, and the per-foot price. Filling it in also sets Number of Bins to match: one bin up to 260 ft, another for every 260 ft after that. Blank leaves both alone.

    The Notes column off the master sheet — the permanent note the crew sees on this house every year, same box as the one in Edit Customer. Blank leaves whatever is already there.

    Type Easy, Medium, Hard, or Unrated — not case-sensitive. This is the same difficulty pill you set on Routes. Blank leaves it unchanged.

    Invoice Fields

    Same idea, for billing info. Matches an existing customer by phone number and creates their invoice — and creates the customer record too if one doesn't exist yet, so nothing lives only in Invoices.

    Duplicate customers

    Finds houses that exist twice — the same customer number, or the same name at the same address — works out which copy to keep, and shows you the whole list. It deletes nothing until you press the second button.

    The copy it keeps is the one carrying the most: an invoice, a place on a route, an address, a pin, a phone. Where both copies carry something the other does not, it refuses to choose and leaves the pair for you.

    Merge duplicates (by name)

    Finds the same customer listed twice under the same name, and combines them into one record instead of just throwing one away. Where one copy has the real address and the other has the price, you end up with a single customer carrying both.

    A field is only ever filled in — anything the kept record already has is never overwritten, so this can add information and cannot lose any. An address of “, UT” counts as no address, so the copy with the real house always wins.

    It stops and asks you when a name has two different customer numbers, two different addresses, or more than one copy already on a route. Changes nothing until you press the second button.

    Danger Zone

    Permanently deletes every customer — their Route entry, their House Map, and their Invoice, all together. This cannot be undone.

    Money already collected stays on the Dashboard permanently, even after a customer is deleted — it's saved separately the moment a payment comes in, so deleting old records never changes what you actually made.

    The permanent bin number. Changing it here puts the old number back in the available pool and takes the new one out, so the pool stays right. A number somebody else already holds is refused — that would leave two bins wearing one label. 5000 and above is the double-bin series; the bin count itself is the box above and is not set for you.

    Health Check

    Looks through your real customers, invoices, routes and quotes for things that don't line up — duplicate numbers, missing invoices, prices that drifted apart, routes pointing at customers who aren't there any more.

    It reads what's already loaded in this page, so running it is free and instant. It changes nothing on its own. Where a problem has one obvious correct fix there's a button; where fixing it means choosing between two valid answers there isn't, because the right call is yours.

    Bulk-Pasting Customers, Routes & Invoices

    That tool lives under Business > Customers > Bulk Updates — paste in columns for names, phones, addresses, and pricing all at once.

    Start the payment log off with what you already have

    Every payment from now on gets its own line — amount, date, method, and who entered it — on the customer’s invoice. Payments taken before that log existed have no line-by-line record: the money is still counted correctly in each customer’s total, there is just nothing showing where it came from.

    This gives each of those customers a single opening balance line, built from what is already on their invoice. Be aware of what that can and cannot be: someone who paid in three instalments becomes one line showing the total and the most recent date, because that is all we ever stored. It is labelled as an opening balance so it can never be mistaken for a real payment record.

    Safe to run more than once — a customer who already has an opening line is skipped.

    Make customer sign-in fast

    A phone number is stored the way the customer typed it — (801) 555-0142 — which the database cannot look up directly. So when someone signs in to the Member Portal, the server has been downloading every customer record to find the one. That is what the “this can take a few seconds” wait on the portal has been.

    This writes a plain, searchable copy of each customer’s phone and email alongside the real ones, so a sign-in reads one record instead of all of them. Nothing a customer or the crew sees changes, and no phone number, email or price is altered — it only adds the tidy copies.

    New and edited customers already get them automatically. This is a one-off for everyone added before now, and it is safe to run more than once.

    Nightly Invoice Automation

    Every night at 7:00 PM, this checks for any house marked Done that hasn't been billed yet — no matter which day it was actually completed, so a house finished late (after 7pm, or the next morning) still gets caught on the very next run instead of getting missed. It automatically emails an invoice — the "Nightly Auto-Invoice — Unpaid" template if they still owe money, or the "Nightly Auto-Invoice — Paid Receipt" template if they're already paid in full. Houses flagged for a fix, or marked "Didn't Get To" by the crew, are skipped and never billed. Each house is only ever billed once, so there's no risk of a repeat send. Edit either template's wording anytime under Templates > Billing.

    After each run you’ll get a text like “23 sent, 0 errors.” If it stops arriving, the run didn’t fire. It’s sent by text (not email), so it reaches you even when email is the problem. Leave blank to turn it off. Send yourself a test with “Send Invoices Now” below to confirm it lands.

    Runs the same billing check right now, on demand — works whether the automatic toggle above is on or off. Use this to send tonight's invoices yourself if you've turned automatic sending off.

    Start New Season

    Run this once when the season starts (around September). It re-opens billing for returning customers: each one owes the same price as last year (dropping the one-time $30 join fee), any old discounts on the invoice are cleared, and their paid amount resets to $0 — after banking last year’s total to your Dashboard so nothing is lost. It also marks them not-yet-installed, so each one bills again automatically the night the crew re-hangs their lights. Customers who said No are left alone.

    Credit already on file for a customer stays and auto-applies. New referral or manual discounts you add ride on top. Running it twice does no harm.

      Responsibilities

      Employees, crews, and daily assignments.

      Employees clock in and out from a separate Crew Portal (a different page, with its own login) that only shows their route, notes, and a clock button — no access to this admin panel. To create an employee login, go to Firebase Console → Authentication → Users → Add User, the same way your own admin login was created.

      Approvals

      Timecard corrections and general requests from the team. Employees marked "Admin" under Employee Names can also approve these from their own portal.

      Timecard Fixes

      Employee Requests

      Employee Categories

      Custom labels like CEO, Warehouse, Sales, or Installers — separate from Role (which controls Crew/route access). An employee can belong to more than one category.

      Employee Names, Role & Pay

      Add each employee's name, then set their Role — Crew for install/fix/removal crews (they get the route map), or a custom label like Warehouse or Receptionist. Position is a free-text job title. Choose Hourly or Salary and enter their pay, and assign them to any Categories above. Below each name, pick exactly which parts of their portal they see.

      Role Templates

      Set up what a job looks like once — like Installer or Office — then just pick that template for each new hire instead of ticking boxes one person at a time. Change the template later and everyone following it updates automatically. Anyone who needs something different can still be customized individually over on Employee Names.

      Time Off Calendar

      Everyone's requested and approved days off in one place. Approved days are filled in, pending days are outlined — click any day to see who's out and approve or deny right there.

      Add Time Off

      Put someone on the calendar yourself — for time off you already agreed to, or days the whole crew is out. Anything added here is approved automatically, and they'll get a notification on their Time Card.

      Leave the last day blank for a single day.

      Requests Without Dates

      Older requests submitted before dates were added, plus anything that isn't day-based. These still need approving from the Approvals list above — they just can't show on the calendar.

      Manage Crews

      Set how many crews you're running, then assign each employee's default crew. Only officially saved crews show here — one-off changes for a single day belong in One-Day Reassignment instead.

      Crew Reassignment

      Move someone to a different crew without changing their usual (saved) crew. Leave "Through" blank for a single day, or set it to keep the change in place for as long as you need — handy when you're covering someone's time off.

      Daily Responsibilities

      For Crew employees, this adds an optional extra checklist on top of their route map. For other roles (Warehouse, Receptionist, etc.), this is their whole day — they'll see just this checklist when they log in.

      Tick the box to mark something done. It's the same checkmark the employee sees on their phone — tick it here or there and it shows done in both places.

      Warehouse

      What needs to be built. This list only fills in automatically when a new install comes from an approved quote. Bulk imports and Member Portal color changes never add anything here on their own — a Member Portal change sends a "Light Color Change" message to Inbox instead (with a feet estimate, if we have one), and you add it below yourself once you've reviewed it. This same list is what warehouse employees see in the Crew Portal.

      For a build request you saw in Inbox, a rebuild, or just buffer stock. Pick the house first — the pattern, the wire and the number of bundles fill themselves in from their record.

      The printed sheet is the same list in the same order, laid out as one row per line with a tick box — so it can be worked down on paper or opened in Excel.

      Fill In Missing Feet

      Fills in Measured Feet for any house that has a price but no measured feet on file, using price ÷ your per-foot rate with a 5% safety margin so estimates lean toward too few feet rather than too many. Never overwrites feet you've already measured.

      Check The Build Queue

      Lists customers who aren't in the build queue, and why — usually missing colours or the build flag turned off.

      Customer Numbers

      Every customer's permanent bin number — single-bin houses pull from the regular sequence, double-bin houses pull from the 5000 series. When a customer is recycled, their number automatically goes back into the available pool.

      Checked and updated automatically every time the app loads — new tests get added and anything that's been fixed moves back to Retest on its own. Your existing results are kept.
      Hand the 0 still-open tests shown to Everything shown here can go out this way - Pass, Fail and N/A have already left this tab.

      Pass, Fail, and N/A tests live here, not on the Test Checklist. Assign a Fail to whoever's fixing it - once it's actually fixed, whoever fixed it (not the office) should mark it Retest, which sends it back to the Test Checklist to run again and drops it off this tab. N/A isn't assigned to anyone - once whatever made it not-applicable changes, mark it Retest the same way. If a fix makes the old test description no longer fit at all, delete this card and add a fresh one instead of forcing a mismatched Retest.

      💳 Payment Integrations

      Choose how customers can pay in the Member Portal. With PayPal selected, customers pay their balance plus an optional tip in one PayPal transaction right on the site, and it's automatically recorded on their invoice the moment they pay — no manual "Mark Paid" needed. Venmo opens the Venmo app with the amount pre-filled, and still has to be marked paid by hand.

      Both shows the Venmo button and the PayPal buttons together and lets the customer pick. PayPal only appears once a Client ID is saved below — so choosing PayPal or Both without one leaves Venmo showing, and a customer is never left with no way to pay.

      This is the public Client ID from your PayPal Developer app (developer.paypal.com → Apps & Credentials) — safe to store here since it's meant to be public. Your Client Secret and Webhook ID are never entered here; those get set up once in Cloud Functions (ask Claude Code to walk you through the terminal commands when you're ready to deploy).
